article_title: Beyond AI Multiples: The Value in Boring Businesses
news_headline: Meta's stock drops on disappointing guidance, dwindling free cash flow
post_text:
Meta reported Q2 revenue of $60.8 billion, up 28% year-over-year, but EPS came in at $6.18 against a $7.22 consensus estimate as costs surged 55%. The sharper number: free cash flow collapsed to $784 million from $8.55 billion a year earlier, even as Meta narrowed its full-year capex guidance to $130-145 billion, roughly double what it spent in all of 2025. Shares fell.

This is what the AI infrastructure arms race looks like from the income statement. The revenue is growing; the cash is disappearing. Across the hyperscaler cohort, Big Tech is collectively on track to spend somewhere between $650 and $725 billion on AI buildout in 2026, and investors are only now starting to ask seriously when any of it pays back.

WBR's piece 'Beyond AI Multiples: The Value in Boring Businesses' makes exactly this case. Capital is chasing AI at premium multiples while patient, cash-generative businesses sit ignored. Meta's quarter is the stress test that argument needed. Read it on the Waterloo Business Review.
